relations.definition: Indicates the geographical location where an event or observation took place.
relations.embedding_query_text: occurred in: Indicates the geographical location where an event or observation took place.

instances: France death rate increase (Public Health) -> France
Paris region death rate increase -> Paris region

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property is a general fit for events occurring in a place, which aligns with the definition and instances.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

relations.definition: Indicates the quantity or value that was observed or documented.
relations.embedding_query_text: recorded: Indicates the quantity or value that was observed or documented.

chosen_property.label: recordedValue
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the quantity or value that was observed or documented.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly captures an event being 'recorded' as a quantity. Minting 'recordedValue' to represent the observed numerical value.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAs
candidates.comment: A recording relation between a music composition and an audio recording of that work. Also called recorded version, audio rendition. Examples: "A music composition 'Symphony No. 5' is recorded as 'Berlin Philharmonic recording'.", "A song 'Yesterday' is recorded as 'The Beatles' original recording'.", "A classical piece is recorded as 'a live performance album'.". Distinct from recordingOf, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: variableMeasured
candidates.comment: A variable measured relation between a dataset or observation and the variables that are measured within it. Also called measured variable, data variable, observation parameter. Examples: "Dataset variableMeasured 'Temperature'", "Observation variableMeasured 'Humidity'", "Dataset variableMeasured 'Patient Age'".

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: collectionSize
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a collection, indicating the total number of items it contains. Also called "number of items", "collection count", "size of collection". Examples: "Art collection collectionSize 500", "Dataset collection collectionSize 10000".

candidates.label: offerCount
candidates.comment: The total number of individual offers aggregated for a product. Also called number of offers, offer quantity, total offers. Examples: "Product A AggregateOffer offerCount 10", "Service B AggregateOffer offerCount 5", "Item C AggregateOffer offerCount 20". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.

candidates.label: reviewCount
candidates.comment: The total number of individual reviews contributing to an aggregate rating. Also called total reviews, number of reviews, review tally. Examples: `Product Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `150`, `Movie Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `5000`, `Service Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `75`.

relations.definition: Specifies the time period or event during which something happened.
relations.embedding_query_text: during: Specifies the time period or event during which something happened.

chosen_property.label: occurredInMonth
chosen_property.definition: Specifies the month during which something happened.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property specifically links an event to a month. Minting 'occurredInMonth'.

chosen_property.label: occurredDuringEvent
chosen_property.definition: Specifies the event during which something happened.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property specifically links an event to another event it occurred during. Minting 'occurredDuringEvent'.

instances: Americans affected by extreme heat -> July Fourth holiday weekend

chosen_property.label: occurredDuringPeriod
chosen_property.definition: Specifies the time period during which something happened.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property specifically links an event to a holiday period. Minting 'occurredDuringPeriod'.

instances: France excess deaths (Public Health) -> 22 and 28 June

chosen_property.label: occurredInDateRange
chosen_property.definition: Specifies the date range during which something happened.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property specifically links an event to a date range. Minting 'occurredInDateRange'.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: duringMedia
candidates.comment: A during media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL representing the circumstances while performing this direction. Also called "instructional media", "step-by-step video", "visual guide". Examples: "How-to direction 'Attach part A' duringMedia 'Video of assembly'", "Direction 'Stir mixture' duringMedia 'Image of stirring technique'".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

relations.definition: Indicates the geographical area or entity for which a forecast is made.
relations.embedding_query_text: forecasted for: Indicates the geographical area or entity for which a forecast is made.

instances: South France temperature forecast -> south of France

chosen_property.label: areaServed
chosen_property.justification: The 'areaServed' property broadly fits the definition of indicating a geographical area for which something is made, like a forecast.

candidates.label: regionsAllowed
candidates.comment: A regions allowed relation between a media object and the geographical areas where its use is permitted. Also called allowed in, permitted regions, geographical availability. Examples: "A movie streaming service has regions allowed 'US, Canada'.", "A music video has regions allowed 'Europe'.", "A software download has regions allowed 'Worldwide'."

candidates.label: areaServed
candidates.comment: An area served relation between a contact point, offer, organization, or service and the geographic region where it is available. Also called service area, coverage region, delivery zone. Examples: "A restaurant's area served is 'Downtown'.", "The delivery service's area served is 'California'.", "An organization's area served is 'Worldwide'."

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: area
candidates.comment: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: shippingDestination
candidates.comment: The specified geographical region or regions where shipping is available or targeted. Also called delivery destination, shipping region, target delivery area. Examples: `Shipping Rate Settings` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: US Postal Codes 90000-90210`, `Offer Shipping Details` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: European Union`, `Delivery Time Settings` shippingDestination `DefinedRegion: North America`. Distinct from `shippingOrigin`, which is where the shipment comes from.

candidates.label: latitude
candidates.comment: A geographical coordinate relation between geo-coordinates or a place and its north-south position on the Earth's surface. Also called lat, north-south coordinate, parallel. Examples: GeoCoordinates have a latitude of '34.0522'. A place has a latitude of '-33.8688'. The city's latitude is '40.7128'. Distinct from longitude, which is the east-west position.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: serviceArea
candidates.comment: The geographical region or area where a service is available or provided. Also called service region, coverage area, operational zone. Examples: `Delivery Service` serviceArea `GeoShape: New York City`, `Local Business` serviceArea `AdministrativeArea: California`, `Customer Support` serviceArea `Place: United States`. Distinct from `areaServed`, which is a more general property for things like organizations.

relations.definition: Indicates the starting time or date of an event or forecast.
relations.embedding_query_text: starts: Indicates the starting time or date of an event or forecast.

instances: Further extreme temperatures forecast -> this weekend

chosen_property.label: startDate
chosen_property.justification: The 'startDate' property directly indicates the beginning date/time of an event or forecast, matching the relation phrase.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.

candidates.label: startOffset
candidates.comment: A temporal offset indicating the start time of a clip or action, measured in seconds from the beginning of a larger work. Also called "clip start time", "beginning offset", "time offset start", "seek start". Examples: "The video clip has startOffset 30 seconds", "The action's startOffset is 120 seconds into the recording", "This segment begins at startOffset 0."

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: opens
candidates.comment: The specific time a place or service opens on a given day or days of the week. Also called opening time, start of business, daily opening hour. Examples: "Monday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '09:00'", "Weekend OpeningHoursSpecification opens '10:00'", "Weekday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '08:30'". Distinct from closes, which specifies the closing time.

relations.definition: Indicates the percentage or amount by which something increased.
relations.embedding_query_text: increased by: Indicates the percentage or amount by which something increased.

instances: France death rate increase (Public Health) -> nearly 30%

chosen_property.label: increasedBy
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the percentage or amount by which something increased.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly captures an increase by a specific percentage. Minting 'increasedBy'.

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: greater
candidates.comment: A greater relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior or larger than another. Also called: is greater than, exceeds, is more than. Examples: "High" greater "Medium", "Excellent" greater "Good", "Large" greater "Small". Distinct from greaterOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: amount
candidates.comment: An amount relation between a financial entity (e.g., loan, grant, money transfer) and the monetary value or number associated with it. Also called value, sum, quantity of money. Examples: "A loan's amount is '$10,000'.", "The grant's amount is '€5,000'.", "A money transfer's amount is '250'."

candidates.label: interestRate
candidates.comment: A financial cost/gain relation between a financial product and the percentage rate of interest charged or paid on it. Also called rate of interest, yield, return rate. Examples: A savings account has an interestRate of '0.5%'. A loan has an interestRate of '4.99%'. A bond has an interestRate of '3.2% fixed'. Distinct from annualPercentageRate, which is the total cost of borrowing over a year, including fees.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: amountOfThisGood
candidates.comment: An amount of this good relation between a type and quantity node and the numerical quantity of a specific good included in an offer. Also called quantity, number of items, item count. Examples: "A shopping cart item's amount of this good is '2'.", "The offer specifies an amount of this good as '5'."

candidates.label: annualPercentageRate
candidates.comment: An annual percentage rate relation between a financial product and the yearly cost of funds, expressed as a percentage, including all fees. Also called APR, yearly interest rate, effective annual rate. Examples: "A loan's annual percentage rate is '5.99%'.", "The credit card's annual percentage rate is '18.5%'."

candidates.label: variesBy
candidates.comment: A varies by relation between a product group and the properties by which its variants differ. Also called variant properties, differentiating attributes, product variations. Examples: "ProductGroup variesBy 'color'", "ProductGroup variesBy 'size'", "ProductGroup variesBy 'material'".

relations.definition: Indicates the source or person who made a statement or claim.
relations.embedding_query_text: stated by: Indicates the source or person who made a statement or claim.

Fires since summer start -> Sebastien Lecornu

chosen_property.justification: The 'spokenByCharacter' property, while typically for fictional characters, can be broadly interpreted to mean 'stated by' a person in this context.

instances: Climate change driving temperatures -> Copernicus climate service
Another heatwave possibility -> Aemet weather service
Anglian Water situation changing -> Anglian Water
UKHSA risks may increase -> UK Health Security Agency

chosen_property.label: creator
chosen_property.justification: The 'creator' property broadly fits for an organization making a statement or forecast, acting as the originator of the information.

instances: Belgium deaths unprecedented -> country's health ministry

chosen_property.label: creator
chosen_property.justification: The 'creator' property broadly fits for a government organization making a statement or observation, acting as the originator of the information.

instances: Death figure an underestimate -> French health minister

chosen_property.label: spokenByCharacter
chosen_property.justification: The 'spokenByCharacter' property, while typically for fictional characters, can be broadly interpreted to mean 'stated by' a person in this context.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: unnamedSourcesPolicy
candidates.comment: An unnamed sources policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a statement about its policy on using unnamed sources. Also called anonymous sources policy, source confidentiality policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "NewsMediaOrganization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/sources-policy'", "Organization unnamedSourcesPolicy 'Our policy requires two independent sources.'", "News outlet unnamedSourcesPolicy 'https://example.com/ethics'".

candidates.label: publishedBy

candidates.label: event

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: timestamp

candidates.label: dissolutionDate

candidates.label: subEvent

candidates.label: recordedAt

candidates.label: commentTime
